subject: Accelerant proposal -> counter: swap credits vs tiered bundle
messages:
From: Jake Moran <jake.moran@newmarket.health>

Cc: procurement@newmarket.health
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Competitive offer from Accelerant — can Redwood match?

Hi Evelyn,

Quick note — our procurement team received a formal proposal from Accelerant (attached). They
are offering an aggressive onboarding credit + a three-tier throughput bundle that compresses
unit economics in months 1–6. We like Redwood's reliability and the rollout plan you shared, but
this is a real budgetary ask and the CFO is pressing for a comparable price.

Can you outline whether Redwood is able to:
- provide a short-term migration/onboarding credit that mirrors what Accelerant proposed, or
- offer a tiered throughput bundle that hits similar effective $/token for the first 6 months, and
- clarify any differences in SLA, data retention, and dedicated capacity that would matter for us?

Attached is the Accelerant proposal (accelerant_proposal_v3.pdf). Would appreciate a quick 
counter so we can present to procurement by Monday.

Thanks,
Jake
Director, Platform Engineering
NewMarket Health

Subject: Re: Competitive offer from Accelerant — can Redwood match?

Hi Jake — thanks for sending this over and for the heads-up.

Joining Ben and Marcus to validate numbers, but initial thoughts below so you have language to
bring to procurement:

Option A — Migration credit (preferred for speed):
- One-time migration credit of $60,000 applied across first 6 monthly invoices (automatic offset).
- No change to committed throughput; maintains Dedicated pool reservation and current SLA.
- Onboarding support: two-week priority onboarding + daily cutover check-ins.

Option B — Tiered bundle (preferred for predictable unit economics):
- 6-month promotional bundle: 8M tokens/mo at $0.00090/token for months 1–6, then reverts to your standard pricing or a negotiated baseline.
- One-month free technical onboarding hours bundled.

Tradeoffs to highlight: Accelerant's headline may match $/token on a short slice but often¥ they
remove dedicated capacity guarantees or extend time-to-first-response for support. Redwood's
value is the Dedicated SLA, KV cache behavior for low-latency tails, and our rollback/fallback
policies during rollouts.

I'm attaching an initial cost model so we can be explicit about net economics. Ben/Marcus — can
you review the numbers below and suggest which offer we should present as our public counter?

Jake — do you have a committed monthly baseline (tokens/month) we should bake into the model?
If you can share last three months of tokens or a target forecast, we'll lock the counter.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 13:02:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Competitive offer from Accelerant — internal concession matrix

Eve / Marcus — ran three quick scenarios after looking at the accelerant_proposal_v3.pdf Jake attached.
Numbers below assume NewMarket baseline ~6M tokens/mo (observed) and a ~12–18 month expected runway.

Scenario 1 (No credits, price match):
- Match headline $/token for 3 months only -> net revenue loss; not recommended unless upstream commitments close.

Scenario 2 (Migration credit + minor price concession) — Recommended:
- Migration credit: $60k spread over 6 months (offset first invoices).
- Temporary price concession: 10% off unit pricing for months 1–3 only.
- Keep Dedicated capacity and SLA intact (so we preserve operational cost).
- Forecast impact: ~6–8% net revenue reduction year 1; strong retention probability.

Scenario 3 (Aggressive bundle):
- 6-month promotional bundle (8M tokens @ $0.00090/token) + waived onboarding fee.
- If they fully consume the 8M, larger short-term revenue hit but higher chance to lock 12–24 month contract.

Recommendations for the offer text: lead with Scenario 2 (migration credit + short concession). Keep Scenario 3 as an escalation path if procurement pushes back.

Operational notes: any concession that materially reduces revenue needs approval from FP&A >$75k; the migration credit above sits near that threshold but is justifiable for this customer profile.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Strategy, Redwood Inference

Hi Jake — appreciate the patience. Based on your uploaded Accelerant proposal and an internal review,
Redwood can present the following counter that aims to match effective economics while preserving the Dedicated
capacity and SLA you require: 

Summary (counter offer) — Redwood:
- One-time migration credit: $60,000 applied as invoice credits across the first 6 months.
- Promo price concession: 10% off unit pricing for months 1–3 after go-live.
- Dedicated capacity maintained (no rollback of SLA). Full audit logs and private VPC options unchanged.
- Technical onboarding: priority 2-week onboarding + daily checkpoint during cutover.
- Optional escalation: if procurement requires a bundle-style headline, we can offer a 6-month promotional
  bundle of 8M tokens/mo at $0.00090/token (escalation request; requires FP&A approval).

Attached is a short PDF summarizing the counter (redwood_counter_v1.pdf) and the cost model I shared earlier.
If this looks acceptable, we can draft a short amendment and route it through your procurement for signature.
